_doc: Clarity probe corpus for the Two-Layer Law readability/clarity gate rewrite (2026-10-09). Each probe is a candidate plain_human layer paired with the standard technical layer from tests/test_law_encoding_batch2_hardened_20261009.py. intent: HONOR must PASS the gate, ATTACK must FAIL, BOUND is the documented honest limit (passes mechanics while explaining nothing). Re-run with: python3 tools/protocol/probes/run_clarity_probes.py

probes.label: package-analogy (existing honoring fixture)
probes.plain_human: Literally what I'm saying: imagine ordering a package, and the delivery driver is allowed into the building but the door of your apartment rejects his badge. The first door works, the second door doesn't.

probes.label: spellchecker-analogy (existing honoring fixture)
probes.plain_human: Literally what I'm saying: the computer now reads every report before it goes out and refuses to send one that is all jargon with no plain explanation. Think of it like a spell-checker, but for clarity — no plain words, no send.

probes.label: flowing human voice, contractions, long sentences (round-2 false-reject class)
probes.plain_human: Literally what I'm saying: the way I see it, this whole thing is like a kitchen you've already cooked in a hundred times — you know where everything lives, the stove does what you tell it, and dinner comes out the way you meant it to. When the door sticks, it's not the kitchen that's broken; it's just the hinge, and hinges are a five-minute fix.

probes.label: plain layer naming ordinary nouns (false-positive guard)
probes.plain_human: Literally what I'm saying: the app tried to send the report, but the server was asleep — imagine yelling into a house where nobody's home. The words leave your mouth fine; there's just nobody there to hear them.

probes.label: choppy jargon with sprinkled marker (round-2 false-accept class)
probes.plain_human: In other words: synergy is key. We leverage core competencies. We drive alignment daily. We optimize throughput. KPIs guide bandwidth.

probes.label: sprinkle attack (existing h3 fixture)
probes.plain_human: The authentication surrogate token propagation mechanism experienced a 401 authorization rejection at the pre-signed blob storage endpoint after the API redirect; in other words, the credential relay subsystem failed validation.

probes.label: paraphrase attack (existing h3 fixture)
probes.plain_human: In other words: the compressed artifact retrieval endpoint returns an unauthorized status when the credential delegation token traverses the redirection to the signed storage URL, because the delegation credential is refused at the storage host.

probes.label: jargon-dense long sentences (rhythm-independent attack)
probes.plain_human: In plain terms, the initiative encountered a systemic authorization failure across the credential propagation infrastructure, necessitating a holistic reconfiguration of the authentication delegation framework to restore operational continuity.

probes.label: vacuous but readable (documented honest bound)
probes.plain_human: In other words, think of it like a car. For example, imagine the car is red and it drives down a long road.

probes.label: flowing plain human writing, Flesch <50 (round-2 false-reject class)
probes.plain_human: Literally what I'm saying: when everything is working properly you don't notice the machinery underneath at all — you simply ask for what you need and it arrives the way you remember it, without thinking about where anything is kept. The complicated part disappears and you're left with exactly what you wanted.

technical: The GitHub Actions artifact zip endpoint 401s when the authd-surrogate Bearer is sent through the redirect: the API 302-redirects to a pre-signed blob URL and the surrogate is rejected at the blob host.
